entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-wrvw-254r-wpmv: CliInvoke.Specializations has command injection in PowerShell and Cmd shell wrappers
entry.content:
CliInvoke.Specializations has command injection in PowerShell and Cmd shell wrappers

Aliases: CVE-2026-100368

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • CliInvoke.Specializations — fixed in 2.8.5
  • CliInvoke.Specializations — fixed in 2.9.4
  • CliInvoke.Specializations — fixed in 2.10.5
  • CliInvoke.Specializations — fixed in 3.0.0-beta.1
  • CliInvoke.Specializations — fixed in 3.0.0-beta.1
  • AlastairLundy.CliInvoke.Specializations — fixed in 2.0.2

### Impact An OS command injection vulnerability exists in the PowerShell and Cmd shell wrappers provided by the `CliInvoke.Specializations` package (the `PowershellProcessInvoker`/`CmdProcessInvoker` invokers, and the `UsePowerShell`/`UseCmd` middleware in v3 pre-release versions). The wrappers re-run a caller-supplied target and arguments inside a shell command (`pwsh -Command ...` / `cmd /c ...`). In affected versions the wrapped command was delivered to the operating system as a single `ProcessStartInfo.Arguments` string. The OS command-line parser re-tokenizes that string before the shell parses it, so a double quote (`"`) in the target or arguments breaks OS-level quoting and lets the wrapped shell reassemble a second, unintended command. An attacker could exploit this to execute …

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-j73w-8hfr-4gc9: CliInvoke: Argument Injection in Extensibility Runner Factory
entry.content:
CliInvoke: Argument Injection in Extensibility Runner Factory

Aliases: CVE-2026-100369

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • CliInvoke — fixed in 2.8.5
  • CliInvoke — fixed in 2.9.4
  • CliInvoke — fixed in 2.10.5
  • CliInvoke — fixed in 3.0.0-beta.2
  • AlastairLundy.CliInvoke — fixed in 2.0.2

### Impact An argument-injection vulnerability exists in the `CliInvoke` package's runner factory: `RunnerProcessFactory` on the 2.x line and `RunnerConfigurationFactory` on the 3.x line. The factory joins the runner arguments, the caller's target, and the caller's arguments into a single `ProcessStartInfo.Arguments` string and hands it to the OS. The OS command-line parser re-tokenizes the string before the runner sees it. A double quote (`"`) in the target or in any argument closes the OS-level quoted region and lets the next character enter argv as a separate element. ### Patches Upgrade to: - **2.8.5** (2.8.x line) - **2.9.4** (2.9.x line) - **2.10.5** (2.10.x line) - **3.0.0-beta.2** (3.x pre-release line) ### Workarounds No complete workaround is available. Until you can upgrade:…

entry.content:
ImageMagick: Memory leak in coders/txt.c without freetype

Aliases: CVE-2026-56371

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • Magick.NET-Q16-AnyCPU — fixed in 14.10.3

  • Magick.NET-Q16-HDRI-OpenMP-arm64 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-HDRI-OpenMP-x64 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-HDRI-arm64 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-HDRI-x64 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-HDRI-x86 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-OpenMP-arm64 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-OpenMP-x64 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-OpenMP-x86 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-arm64 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-x64 — fixed in 14.10.3

If a `texture` attribute is specified for a TXT file, an attempt will be made to read it via `texture=ReadImage(read_info,exception);`. Later, when retrieving metrics via the `GetTypeMetrics` function, if this function fails (i.e., `status == MagickFalse`), the calling function will exit immediately but fail to release the texture object, leading to memory leakage.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-2gq3-ww97-wfjm: ImageMagick has a possible heap Use After Free vulnerability in its meta coder
entry.content:
ImageMagick has a possible heap Use After Free vulnerability in its meta coder

Aliases: CVE-2026-56376

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L

Affected:

  • Magick.NET-Q16-AnyCPU — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-HDRI-AnyCPU — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-HDRI-OpenMP-arm64 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-HDRI-OpenMP-x64 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-HDRI-arm64 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-HDRI-x64 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-HDRI-x86 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-OpenMP-arm64 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-OpenMP-x64 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-OpenMP-x86 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q16-arm64 — fixed in 14.10.3
  • Magick.NET-Q8-AnyCPU — fixed in 14.10.3

A heap Use After Free vulnerability exists in the meta coder when an allocation fails and a single byte is written to a stale pointer. ``` ==535852==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free on address 0x5210000088ff at pc 0x5581bacac14d bp 0x7ffdf667edf0 sp 0x7ffdf667ede0 WRITE of size 1 at 0x5210000088ff thread T0 ```
